record.what_it_does: Spreadsheet-database platform for building collaborative apps, workflows and tables.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (code_challenge is the SHA-256 of code_verifier). Access tokens expire after 60 minutes. Refresh tokens are valid for 60 days and rotate on each use, so authorizations can be refreshed indefinitely. Personal access tokens are scoped by permission and by base or workspace, are created at /create/tokens, and are sent as Bearer tokens. Enterprise admins can create PATs for service accounts. Legacy user API keys can no longer be created.
record.access_notes: Any account, free ones included, can create PATs and register OAuth integrations. No plan restriction is stated for PATs. Before other users can authorize an OAuth integration, the developer must add a support email, privacy policy URL and terms of service URL. The OAuth guide mentions no review or approval step. Usage is capped by plan: Free allows 1,000 API calls per workspace per month, Team 100,000, and Business is unlimited. Rate limits are 5 req/s per base and 50 req/s per user for PAT traffic. Enterprise-admin, SCIM, audit-log and eDiscovery endpoints need Enterprise Scale.
record.api_breadth_notes: The developer llms.txt index lists about 98 endpoint pages. They cover records CRUD and CSV sync, attachment upload, comments, bases, tables, fields and views metadata, webhooks (6 operations), collaborators, invites, shares and workspaces, HyperDB, plus enterprise users, audit logs, eDiscovery and SCIM. About half are Enterprise-only admin endpoints. The core data API is about 30-40 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Airtable hosts an official MCP server at https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp. It authenticates with OAuth or a PAT and is available on all plans (support article "Using the Airtable MCP server"). Community servers also exist, such as domdomegg/airtable-mcp-server.
record.blocker_notes: There is no blocker for building. Users on the Free plan are capped at 1,000 API calls per workspace per month, which limits heavy agent use. Webhooks created with PAT or OAuth tokens expire after 7 days unless refreshed or their payloads are listed. Webhook notifications are pings containing only the base and webhook IDs, so payloads must be fetched separately. Airtable publishes no official OpenAPI spec. There is no dedicated sandbox, so a free account serves as the dev environment.
